item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Typowriter
item.description: Reality bender that changes things through creating typos in text that it copies from exterior sources
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Highly powerful reality bender manifesting in the form of a common typewriter. The typewriter will essentially create "transcripts" of nearby media, although it often makes typos. If a typo happens to create a sentence in the transcript that grammatically makes sense, it will become reality. It runs forever and will make increasingly more typos on a transcript if the same piece of media is shown to it multiple times.

Central Narrative: I plan for this to be an SCP that has been in containment for awhile, however without any reliable containment procedures. There will be an extensive list of research notes and observations about the operations of SCP XXXX. The main "narrative" stems from a recovered journal. The SCP is contained by singing up 4 unwitting rural towns to use their local news stations, newspapers, and radio broadcasts for SCP XXXX. Although MTFs patrol all 4 towns constantly, one woman begins to keep a journal of all the weird alterations that happen, so she can be sure she isn't going crazy (as the towns are frequently amnestizied due to the SCP)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Completely random reality bender that is able to warp anything by writing a typo

Additional Notes: The reality anchors do not work on this SCP, in actuality because it kills some of the fun associated with it. I think a decent theory within the narrative as to why this is so is that SCP XXXX is a recovered byproduct of SCP 3812 (SCP-3812)

item.title: [Feedback request] Enigma Dilemma
item.description: Some weapons of war become more dangerous as centuries pass.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unsure, guidance requested

Elevator Pitch: An 18th century naval war table that displays the location of every military vessel currently on water in the world.

Central Narrative: The war table is suspected to have been made during the American Revolution*, leading to many of the naval battles of the war ending in British defeat despite their superiority on sea. It is also thought to have been used in the battles of Manila Bay (1898) and Coronel (1914), as well as many decisive (and unlikely) engagements in WWII. Following the war, the object was considered displaced and eventually lost until resurfacing in the continental US some 50 years later. Through unclear means, it had ended up in an antique shop where its outrageous price had scared off any buyers for years until the Foundation's involvement.

*the nature of the Battle of Quiberon Bay in 1759 has raised concerns regarding the object's assumed creation date.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The title of this thread: an Enigma dilemma. In WWII, Britain cracked the Enigma cipher. However, using this to save every Allied naval convoy from U-boats would have made it obvious to the Germans that their cipher has been cracked, and so Allied command was faced with a question: you know where, what, and when the enemy will strike. Which attacks do you let happen and which attacks do you thwart?

This SCP is a similar question but on a far larger scale; every public, secret, and clandestine naval movement is laid bare. Any naval force secretly moving against another would force the international, humanity-shielding Foundation to either pick sides, or let conflict after conflict happen. With what could happen if it fell into the wrong hands, and with GOIs interested in acquiring the object, securing, containing, and protecting is very literal.

Additional Notes: This would be my first contribution to the site and as such, I would appreciate thorough criticism. There are currently no drafts and I am not counting on this being approved or greenlit, though that would be a nice surprise. Additionally, I'd like some help with the genres—or is History alone enough?

item.title: The Nanny
item.description: A mysterious creature who 'cares' for its victims
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

  • An entity that refers to itself as the Nanny.
  • capable of producing a thick fog around it. Lives in a marshland in the south of England.
  • It tries to lure people towards it with glowing globules of light. Once a person reaches it, it will proceed to ask them to tea, to play some games or have their medicine (other things as well). Keeps the person captive performing perversions of nanny-care. For example, feeding someone their medicine might be pushing mud into their mouth or giving them tea might be feeding them mud and rocks. It essentially tries to immobilise them under the ruse of caring for them.
  • Once they have been deemed to have sufficiently cared for, the nanny takes them to a place it refers to as 'the garden' (is a recession in the ground with various pods and bulbs hanging on the walls) there it introduces them to the 'other children' which appear to be larvae or younglings of this creature who then devour the human.

Central Narrative: D-class sent into the marsh, discover the nanny and are brought to the garden, try escaping. Reveals other ability of the SCP, has full control over the location, temperature and density of the fog around it. Used to help catch prey or defend itself.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An entity that lures people with lights sort of like an angler fish, also similar to will'o'wisps which could explain the folklore in that area.

Additional Notes: NONE

item.title: "God Bless Americana Anómalos" Idea Critique Request
item.description: The American Flag was a plant all along.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout:

  • ConProcs
  • Description
  • Discovery Log
  • List of SCP-Events
  • Testing Logs
  • Interview and Final Word from O5

Elevator Pitch:

You're home alone, watching the tv of your country. You hear a noise in the other room and go to investigate. You see nothing but the American flag planted firmly in the center of the room.

Then a voice whispers to you

"God bless America".

And then you start a revolution.

-Marcelles_Raynes 12/4/2020

1 out of every 5,000 American flags is a sentient petal of an extra-dimensional plant that symbiotically infects humans (mostly foreigners) and puppets them into influencing the political state of America with non-anomalous memetic strategies.

Story and Hook +
Story and Hook -

Central Narrative: The first American flag, the original progenitor of this SCP, inspired the American Revolution only because the east coast was the perfect habitat for it to grow. The anomaly successfully thrived in America for centuries undetected, keeping their percentage of American hosts lower than the percentage of non-American hosts globally. And while these flags are too light to stop the wind from pushing them around outside, inside the human body they can morph themselves into microscopic threads to navigate, manipulate their hosts, and avoid detection.

It isn’t until 2015, when the Bundy standoff between the BLM and the ATF revealed a new progenitor flag attempting to start another revolution, that the Foundation identifies the presence of the anomaly. While the Foundation realizes complete containment of the anomaly would force them and the US into open war, they also discover that the anomaly has been defending humanity from numerous shape-shifting anomalies in secret, making itself essential to their needs too. They accept that the anomaly cannot and does not need to be actively contained, so, with caution, they focus on the threat of wild American flags going rogue and starting a new America all over again.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Inspired by a comment made by Marcelles_Raynes 's perspective on the phrase “God Bless America,” this SCP focuses on highlighting and mocking much of American flavored jingoism while not explaining it all off as something completely unnatural.

Johnny Appleseed, tea dumping in the Boston river, the start of the Spanish-American war, Westerns, and others are given are both humorous and unsettling examples. Test logs show how flags choose/infect their host and how infected hosts take down other shape-shifting threats (hint: think of a "pulling a handkerchief out of the mouth" magic trick but deadly.) Also hints at the end about what might have O5 worried most of all about the anomalies freedom.

Additional Notes: The title is supposed to be the genus and species name but correct me if I got the order or idea wrong. Thanks!

item.title: Looking for Greenlight on fungal SCP
item.description: Infectious disease anomaly with what I believe to be a unique twist on the topic.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout:
Containment Procedures. There will be two sections - Original Containment and Revised Containment Procedures.
Description.
Addendums. Consists of short emails, lab reports, and mission transcripts. Will be how the “meat” of the narrative is told by leading the reader along a trail of breadcrumbs.

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a collective term for a genus of Glomeromycota (soil-borne fungi). A type of endoparasite only found in remote, humid environments within the latitudes of 23.5 N(Tropic of Cancer) and 23.5 S (Tropic of Capricorn), it infects organisms belonging to the order of Primates.

SCP-XXXX-1a refers to organisms infected with SCP-XXXX spores. Instances go through 3 stages of infection and are considered “mature” once they enter the fourth. Mature instances can reproduce SCP-XXXX by releasing spores. Has significant regenerational properties of interest to the Foundation as a result of SCP-XXXX “grafting” plant onto animal cells as it takes over the hosts’ body.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-1b refers to cocoons of inactive 1a instances. Since 1a instances use sunlight to metabolize ATP (which are essentially walking plants made of fungi), they enter a sort of hibernation when deprived of it by encasing themselves in calcified plant matter. If left for too long become 1c instances.

SCP-XXXX-1c instances are large fungal umbrella shaped bodies approximately three (3) meters in height and bioluminescent in color. The majority of its surface is covered in microscopic cilia specialized in capturing fungal spores from its immediate atmosphere. Furthermore, SCP-XXXX-1c is capable of accelerating abnormal amounts of fungal growth in its vicinity, creating entirely new ecosystems of toxic bioluminescent fungi. These new environments are referred to as SCP-XXXX-1d. SCP-XXXX spores are common around 1c and throughout 1d.

Bioluminescent fungi in SCP-XXXX-1d emit a fruity aroma that compels the victim to consume it. This effect is exponential over long periods of time, therefore classifying 1c and 1d instances as cognitohazards. Once ingested orally, victims fall into a coma, making them susceptible to infection via SCP-XXXX-1a instances

Central Narrative:
The Foundation tries to study an anomaly that could have medical benefits for personnel on the field if thoroughly understood. The site director, assigned to study the anomaly after recent failures in his own work, sees this as a chance to make his comeback. However, he, in in his pursuit to do so, unknowingly forces the anomaly through “artificial selection” (a process in which humans breed animals/plants in order to obtain offspring with certain traits), making the anomaly in general much more dangerous and difficult to contain than it originally was.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Humans make mistakes. We misjudge things which, ultimately, may end up making the situation worse. The Foundation is, at least partly, run by humans, and is therefore not exempt from this fact.

item.description: A sewing needle that transfer negative emotions to garments
item.content:encoded:
A sewing needle that transfer negative emotions to garments, which in turn magnify and transfer them to the wearer.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): n/a

Elevator Pitch: Any instance of an otherwise ordinary sewing needle that transfers the negative thoughts and emotions of the user into the garment/item the needle is used to make or repair, but only when the the person sewing pricks their finger with the needle and draws blood. The garment/item then imparts those same negative thoughts and emotions, magnified several times over, into the end user of the created item. Items created with the needle retain those properties indefinitely, and have the ability to impart the same properties of the original needle onto any new needle that is used to alter or repair them, again with the requirement that the person using the needle pricks their finger and draws blood.

Central Narrative: From a story perspective, I plan for the article to contain incident reports with references to various historical events, with pieces of clothing of key participants in those events having been affected by the needle.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Has the ability to self propagate, though only under specific circumstances. This prevents it from being overpowered, while allowing instances to remain hidden in plain site for extended periods of time. The same applies to any items created with the needle, leading to sporadic “outbreaks” of items created with instances of the needle that must be responded to by the Foundation.

item.title: (Looking for greenlight) Ancient elevators
item.description: Historical anomaly in which the electric elevator originates from 3000 BC
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy / Bizarre (if that counts as a category)

Elevator Pitch:

  • According to the public, the elevator was invented and popularized in the late 1800's.
  • In actuality, the first elevators popped up around 3000 BC.
  • Functional elevators can be found in historic buildings; there's even ancient Egyptian elevators in the great pyramids.

Central Narrative:
The containment procedures and description serve to introduce the anomaly and explain how the Foundation is handling it. The Foundation puts out the story that the first elevator was installed in 1880, and whenever they find an elevator created before that date, they either destroy it, conceal it, or make it look like a modern elevator. It also serves to justify some aspects of the anomaly, like how elevators could be invented before electricity, or how knowledge of how to build an elevator could propagate in the first place.

+ show block
– hide block

Then there's an addendum explaining some notable examples of ancient elevators, which serve both to clarify the anomaly further and act as their own interesting anecdotes. Examples I have in mind are solid stone elevators installed into the great pyramids, how elevators are used in various medieval castles, and possibly even mentions of elevators in the bible.

The resolution to the SCP comes in the form of an MTF log. Foundation satellites detect an object manifest in space and slowly descend to the earth's surface. An MTF squad is deployed to the estimated landing zone, and discover it to be a descending elevator. When it hits the surface, aliens pop out, and explain that 4000 yeas ago, they gave the gift of elevators to man, having misinterpreted instructions from the alien queen to "uplift" our species.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
It might be ambitious for a first SCP, but if I go with the "aliens taught us how to make elevators" story, the hook could be that the object class is Explained, with the subclass of Keter, since even though the anomaly is explained the phenomenon still requires coverup procedures.

Alternatively, the hook could just be an incredibly jarring phrase in the containment procedures, like "Highly visible elevators installed in notable historic sites, such as the main lobby elevator of the Great Pyramid of Giza…".

Additional Notes:
Some of my favorite SCPs are the ones that are just about something straight up bizarre, like 5940 or 5319 or 2598 or 4062. Something about them appeals to me in a huge way, more than horror or drama ever does in SCPs. It's definitely what I wanna try for my first SCP, if it wouldn't be too much of a challenge.

item.title: The Recursive Dollhouse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fridge Horror/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: Essentially, SCP-XXXX a dollhouse of whatever environment it is currently being contained within. Likewise, it would sustain a diminished capability of whatever building it is housed in. SCP-XXXX-1 are essentially "dolls" housed in the facility that make up sentient/concious organisms. This also applies to anomalous materials as well, such as me, the toaster that speaks in the first person or the mask SCP. In addition, the anomalous effects of objects are still maintained but to a much smaller degree. Objects within the SCP-XXXX move in tandem with their current reality counterparts. Actions made within the main facility are mirrored in SCP-XXXX. There is in fact a miniature version of SCP-XXXX (dubbed SCP-XXXXa) and it is theorized that there are multiple versions of SCP-XXXX that exist within the dimensional realm.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation found this dollhouse in the middle of a nursery amongst other toys. After examining this, an entity attempts to contact them (potentially, though I am not sold on the concept) in an attempt to get it back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The inherent dread of a recursive universe where what we view from within could in fact be caused by an upper plane of existence is terrifying, no?

Additional Notes: Edit 1: As for what happens when objects or instances of SCP-XXXX-1 are affected by outside users, I'd like to go into that further within test logs potentially. If not, essentially, the-what I dub-"dollhouse reality" can be affected by users. The current reality would be marginally affected in a similar manner. This isn't compulsory, however, but it does bring about satisfaction of the affected individual to complete said task. Other more violent actions such as the destruction of an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 can cause a severely minimized effect on the affected individual.If an anomalous SCP-XXXX-1 instance comes in contact with a non-anomalous instance of SCP-XXXX-1, the effects that would be generated by the anomalous instance are greatly minimized. Objects brought into the SCP-XXXX reality will manifest in the current reality as well.

Third knob has 'Manual' option to manually use the machine, 'Automatic' option to create the desired outcome (input through speaking to machine) like a 3D printer and a 'Learning' option which makes the machine experiment with its own design and material used, creating some funky and inventive clothing items. Owners seized machine after the occupant, wealthy English woman Ollie Mae Price, went missing for more than 14 days. Owners were intrigued but could not figure out how to use the machine. Experimented with it and created a bra made of wool whilst using the automatic setting. Owners then made bras out of glass and porcelain. Began to sell the pieces on a street stall, stirring widespread rumours that ultimately reached The Foundation. Foundation questioned the owners briefly, dispensing Class B amnestics after seizing the machine. Foundation found some people from Dharavi wearing purple-dyed metallic shirts, coats and skirts. Suspicions arose that Ollie had been supplying clothes made by the machine to the Dharavian citizens for an unknown, possibly benevolent reason. Foundation now has an immense interest in the machine to efficiently create armours as well as replace lose laundry. Foundation interviews the machine to explore its origin, creator as well as the whereabouts of Ollie and what her motives were with the machine. Hook/Attention-Grabber: The endless possibilities and uses The Foundation has with the machine, much like SCP-294. The machine's 'learning' feature establishes its own growth as an entity and how it is gaining knowledge and changing before The Foundation's eyes.

The other common feature shared is that despite being composed of normal human bone composition (Collagen and Calcium Phosphate) they are extremely indestructible, except to electricity ranging from two thousand to four thousand (2000-4000) volts.
This incapacitates the entities, therefore tesla gates are positioned outside their containment cells. Safe/Euclid classification is an ongoing decision as they seem to use their abilities for the good of the world, but this could just be a publicity stunt to trick the foundation.

Central Narrative: The Story with these anomalies is that they were found in a cave in outer London, and DNA tests suggests they were part of the royal family in 15th century Britain.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There isn't much special about the premise of SCP-5672 apart from the anomalies abilities, which were thought to be obtained by strange minerals and substances in a cave under London.

Additional Notes: Caesium-135 and Strontium-99 were found in small traces near the cave entrance. This suggests prolonged exposure to radioactive material, but no nuclear bomb/accident has occurred in the UK.

Elevator Pitch: Put simply, SCP-XXXX is a cat-like apparition which consumes souls. It once had intangibility (Which it lost during an incident), and it can shield itself from all wavelengths of light, rendering itself invisible for a short duration.

It’s a hunter, so it stalks any kind of prey which catches its interest, though it prefers humans. It will stalk its target, memorizing all of its routines, mannerisms, and daily patterns in extreme detail. When they are at a point of vulnerability (Provided SCP-XXXX hasn’t lost interest) it will consume their soul.

After a large amount of souls are consumed, it exhales them into the form of a polychromatic sphere, which it then carries to an unidentifiable and unspecified location.

+ Show block
- Hide block

That’s how it’s going to be written, but in actuality, SCP-XXXX is bringing the sphere to a GOI (Of my creation) so they can use it to prevent some kind of cataclysmic event from occuring. The Foundation is unaware of this, and all they know is that whenever they try to take the sphere away from the SCP, several events occur:

  1. SCP-XXXX becomes extremely agitated.
  2. People start disappearing from the Foundation (They’re actually being dragged away by a hand of the SCP which actually causes the cataclysmic event.)
  3. Emergence of multiple anomalous entities appearing all over the world
  4. Cataclysmic event occurs.

Central Narrative: It’s a question of morals. The Foundation has to escort SCP outside after it creates the sphere (Which can even be a problem at times), but each time it’s outside it also does what it wants, and consumes even more souls. Even though the SCP’s job is presumably important, is it morally correct for the Foundation to just let it go around killing people?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Since the SCP has lost its intangibility and is now at odds with the Foundation, this prompts it to use its superior intelligence to resist and counteract any new containment procedures that the Foundation tries to come up with.

It is only accessible by a junction located a few miles from the Southeastern entrance of the Bradway Tunnel in South Yorkshire. Inside the yard, there are about 50 sidings and 14 entryways (9 of which lead to tunnels) and two operating facilities. Surrounding the yard is a rocky, heathland similar to those found in the UK.

On some occasion, locomotives enter the railyard via the tunnels or junctions. Locomotives of all kinds will enter and exit the railyard and will only remain to dispatch/pick up all cargo. The only locomotives permanently found within are a GWR 9400 Class and two BR Class 10.

Central Narrative: The junction was initially found in 1965 during the Beeching Axe. Reports came in of workers vanishing when they attempted to find the end of the line. The Foundation came in when a BR DMU went missing along with 37 passengers.

In the penultimate log, it mentions a 'smoke' engine exiting the junction, with four humans on board. Later, during an interview with one of the humans, she reveals to be one of the passengers who went missing on the BR DMU a few years before.
